source_text: 26 STULTE NON PERMORERIS DEO. Stulte, non permoreris nec mortuus effugis actus, Tu licet disponas nihil te sentire defuncto. Uinceris, insipiens: uiuit Deus conditor orbis, Legitima cuius clamat ualere defuncto. Tu autem dum praeceps sine Deo uiuere quaeris, Extinctum in fatis iudicas aut fatale credis. Non ita disposuit, ut tu putas, Deus aeternus, Obliuitos esse mortuos de gesto priore. Nunc nobis imperita fecit receptacula mortis, Post cineres autem nostros uidebimus illa. Erue te, stulte, qui putas, post funera non sis. Rectorem dominumque tuum nihil posse fecisti. Mors autem in uacuum non est, si corde retractes. Optandum noscas, nam sero senties illum. Rector eras carnis, non te certe caro regebat; Exemptus ab illa reconditur illa tuorum. Recte mortalis homo separatur a carne. Idcirco nec poterint oculi mortales aequare, Sic habet abyssus noster de Dei secreta. Da nunc ergo Deo, fragilis dum moreris, honorem, Et crede, quod Christus uiuum te de mortuo reddit. Omnipotenti laudes in ecclesia reddere debes. [27] Trade te iam Christo, ut te benefacta sequantur.
pass_a_gloss: 26 Fool not you-will-die-utterly before-God. Fool, not you-will-die-through nor as-dead you-escape deeds… Give now therefore to-God, fragile while you-die, honor, and believe that Christ living you from dead returns. To-Almighty praises in church to-return you-ought. [27] Hand-over yourself already to-Christ, that you good-deeds may-follow.

pass_b_english: Instruction 26 — Fool, you do not perish utterly before God. Fool, you will not die through and through, nor as a dead man escape your deeds — even if you arrange to feel nothing once you have died. You are beaten, senseless one: the God who founded the world lives, whose lawful claims cry out that they still hold for the dead. While you rush to live without God, you judge a person extinguished in the fates, or you believe it is fate. The eternal God did not arrange it as you think — that the dead are forgetful of what they did before. He has now made for us the holding-places of death for the unskilled; but after our ashes we will see those things. Tear yourself free, fool, who think that after the funeral you are not. You have made out that your Ruler and Lord can do nothing. But death is not into a void, if you turn it over in the heart. Know what should be hoped for — for late you will feel him.

You were ruler of the flesh; certainly the flesh was not ruling you. Freed from it, that flesh of yours is stored away. Rightly is a mortal human separated from flesh. Therefore mortal eyes will not be able to match this — so deep is our abyss concerning God’s secrets. So now, while you are fragile and dying, give honor to God, and believe that Christ makes you alive again from the dead. You ought to return praises to the Almighty in the church.
Instruction 27 (close): Hand yourself over to Christ already, so that good deeds may follow you.
